narrative:
The 2026 Houston Astros entered the season carrying the weight of a dynasty that had begun to gray at the temples. Veterans like Jose Altuve and Yordan Alvarez were still capable of brilliance, but a brutal April — going just 8-18 — exposed how thin the margin for error had become. The pitching staff leaked runs at an alarming rate, and the lineup, despite its star power, could not keep pace. April felt less like a stumble and more like a warning that this version of the Astros was genuinely vulnerable.

The calendar turned, and so did Houston's fortunes. From May through July, the Astros steadily clawed their way back to relevance. Cam Smith emerged as a legitimate force, Joey Loperfido delivered a stunning clutch home run in late June, and Yordan Alvarez's grand slam on the final day of June felt like a punctuation mark on a remarkable recovery. The team went 44-35 over those three months, transforming a season that looked lost into one teetering on the edge of something meaningful. It was not always pretty — the pitching staff continued to bleed — but the offense carried the load.

August and September told a more complicated story. Christian Walker and Daulton Varsho provided heroics in mid-August, and Cam Smith's 20th home run in September underscored his breakthrough campaign. But Bryan Abreu's inability to hold a lead against Atlanta in late September — surrendering a Ronald Acuña Jr. grand slam — symbolized the fragility of a rotation and bullpen that had been patched together all year. The Astros finished exactly 81-81, a coin-flip team that somehow willed itself into the postseason.

The Wild Card round against what appeared to be a scrappy Boston squad proved to be the Astros' final act. Bryan King's relief work was shaky throughout the series, and while Altuve and Cam Smith hit postseason home runs to keep hope alive, the bullpen could not protect leads. Chase Meidroth's three-run homer off Bryan Abreu in Game 2 was the killing blow, and Houston's season ended with Alvarez lining out and Altuve flying out in the final frame — veterans swinging at a dynasty's last breath.

chapters.title: April Freefall
chapters.description: A brutal 8-18 April puts Houston in an early grave, defined by defensive miscues and pitching that cannot hold leads.

chapters.title: Fighting Back
chapters.description: Cam Smith and the offense spark a May recovery, turning a lost season into a legitimate playoff chase.

chapters.title: The Summer Surge
chapters.description: A run of clutch June performances — Loperfido's walk-off blast, Altuve's three-run shot, Alvarez's grand slam — elevates Houston into contention.

chapters.title: Holding On
chapters.description: August heroics from Walker and Varsho keep the Astros above water, but a late-September Acuña grand slam off Abreu foreshadows the cracks ahead.

chapters.title: October's Last Stand
chapters.description: Houston's Wild Card run produces fleeting moments of Altuve and Smith magic before the bullpen surrenders the series and the dynasty's era quietly closes.
